messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Japanese, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Japanese line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.
そう、私の魂は、まだ飛び続けていた、 後ろへ振り返り、道を再び見つめた その峠を、生きた者が今まで一度も離れたことはなかった。

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

**Word‑to‑Japanese Mapping Table**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Word / Phrase | Back‑Translation (Japanese → English) | Status | |-------------|----------------------|----------------------|----------------------------------------|--------| | così | “so … that” (resultative) | そう | “so / thus” | OK | | l'animo | “the soul” (subject) | 魂は | “(the) soul (topic)” | OK | | mio | possessive “my” | 私の | “my” | OK | | ch'ancor | relative “which still” | まだ | “still / yet” | OK | | fuggiva | imperfect “was fleeing / flying” | 飛び続けていた | “was continuing to fly” | OK | | si | reflexive clitic (self‑directed) | — | (reflexivity is implicit in 振り返り) | **UNNECESSARY** | | volse | “turned (back)” | 振り返り | “turned back / looked back” | OK | | a (1) | preposition in “a retro” (direction) | へ | “to / toward” (as part of 後ろへ) | **UNNECESSARY** | | retro | “back” (direction) | 後ろ | “back / behind” | OK | | a (2) | infinitival marker “to” (purpose) | — | (purpose expressed by verb form 見つめた) | **UNNECESSARY** | | rimirar | “to look again” | 見つめた | “looked at / gazed at” | OK | | lo | definite article “the” (masc.) | — | (article omitted in Japanese) | **UNNECESSARY** | | passo | “the pass” (object) | 道 | “the road / path” | OK | | che | relative pronoun “which” | その | “that / the” | OK | | non | negation “not / never” | なかった (part of 離れたことはなかった) | “did not” | OK | | lasciò | “left / departed” | 離れた | “left / departed” | OK | | già | “already” (temporal emphasis) | 今まで | “until now / already” | OK | | mai | “never” (intensifier) | 一度も | “not even once / never” | OK | | persona | “person” (human) | 者 | “person / one” | OK | | viva | “living” (adjective) | 生きた | “living / alive” | OK |

### Items Requiring Attention - **UNNECESSARY**: *si*, *a* (both occurrences), *lo* – these Italian grammatical particles have no direct counterpart in Japanese and are naturally omitted. - No **MISSING**, **WRONG**, or **GRAMMAR** issues were found; all remaining source words are adequately rendered in the Japanese translation.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. Verify that the output contains only Japanese script; no other language scripts should be mixed in. Output format (use nested bullet list, not table): - Line N: - Original: ... - Issue: ... (or "none") - Corrected: ... (or "no change") Output final Japanese text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).

- **Line 25** - Original: そう、私の魂は、まだ飛び続けていた、 - Issue: 余分な読点「、」が「そう」の後にある。 - Corrected: そう私の魂は、まだ飛び続けていた、
- **Line 26** - Original: 後ろへ振り返り、道を再び見つめた - Issue: 内部に読点があり、対象が「道」になっている。 - Corrected: 後ろへ振り返り峠を再び見つめた
- **Line 27** - Original: その峠を、生きた者が今まで一度も離れたことはなかった。 - Issue: 内部に読点がある。 - Corrected: 峠は生きた者が今まで一度も離れたことはなかった。
``` そう私の魂は、まだ飛び続けていた、 後ろへ振り返り峠を再び見つめた 峠は生きた者が今まで一度も離れたことはなかった。 ```
